/-!
# Harborth's conjecture

Harborth's conjecture states that every planar graph can be drawn with integer edge lengths:
every (finite, simple) planar graph has a planar drawing in the Euclidean plane in which every
edge is a straight line segment of integer length. Such a drawing is also called an
*integral Fáry embedding*, since (if true) the conjecture strengthens Fáry's theorem on the
existence of planar straight-line drawings.

Mathlib has no notion of a planar graph, so this file defines planar drawings explicitly.
A *planar drawing* of a graph maps vertices to distinct points of the plane and edges to simple
arcs joining the images of their endpoints, so that an arc contains no vertex other than its
endpoints and two distinct arcs meet only in common endpoints. A graph is *planar* if it has a
planar drawing. A *planar straight-line drawing* is a planar drawing in which the arc of every
edge is the closed segment between the images of its endpoints.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Harborth's conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harborth%27s_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in
  mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [KH01] Kemnitz, A. and Harborth, H., *Plane integral drawings of planar graphs*,
  Discrete Mathematics 236 (2001), 191–195.
  [doi:10.1016/S0012-365X(00)00442-8](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0012-365X(00)00442-8)
-/

structure IsPlanarDrawing (f : V → ℝ²) (arc : Sym2 V → Set ℝ²) : Prop where
  injective : Function.Injective f
  exists_path : ∀ u v, G.Adj u v →
    ∃ γ : Path (f u) (f v), Function.Injective γ ∧ Set.range γ = arc s(u, v)
  notMem_arc : ∀ u v w, G.Adj u v → w ≠ u → w ≠ v → f w ∉ arc s(u, v)
  inter_subset : ∀ u v u' v', G.Adj u v → G.Adj u' v' → s(u, v) ≠ s(u', v') →
    arc s(u, v) ∩ arc s(u', v') ⊆ f '' (({u, v} : Set V) ∩ {u', v'})

Mathlib's `Path` and `segment` are reused.

blocks.name: IsPlanarDrawing
blocks.text:
/--
`IsPlanarDrawing G f arc` says that `f` and `arc` form a planar drawing of `G` in the plane:
* the vertices are mapped injectively to points `f v` of the plane;
* the edge `s(u, v)` is drawn as the set `arc s(u, v)`, which is a simple arc from `f u` to `f v`,
  i.e. the range of an injective path from `f u` to `f v`;
* the arc of an edge passes through no vertex other than its two endpoints;
* the arcs of two distinct edges meet only in the images of their common endpoints.
-/
structure IsPlanarDrawing (f : V → ℝ²) (arc : Sym2 V → Set ℝ²) : Prop where
  injective : Function.Injective f
  exists_path : ∀ u v, G.Adj u v →
    ∃ γ : Path (f u) (f v), Function.Injective γ ∧ Set.range γ = arc s(u, v)
  notMem_arc : ∀ u v w, G.Adj u v → w ≠ u → w ≠ v → f w ∉ arc s(u, v)
  inter_subset : ∀ u v u' v', G.Adj u v → G.Adj u' v' → s(u, v) ≠ s(u', v') →
    arc s(u, v) ∩ arc s(u', v') ⊆ f '' (({u, v} : Set V) ∩ {u', v'})

@[category API, AMS 5 52]
theorem exists_path_segmentArcs {f : V → ℝ²} (hf : Function.Injective f) {u v : V}
    (huv : G.Adj u v) :
    ∃ γ : Path (f u) (f v), Function.Injective γ ∧ Set.range γ = segmentArcs f s(u, v) :=
  ⟨Path.segment (f u) (f v), fun _ _ h => Subtype.ext <|
    AffineMap.lineMap_injective ℝ (hf.ne huv.ne) (by simpa using h), by simp⟩
blocks.docstring:

images of its endpoints, so the `exists_path` condition of `IsPlanarDrawing` is automatic for
straight-line drawings.

@[category test, AMS 5 52]
theorem harborths_conjecture_completeGraph_fin_two :
    ∃ f : Fin 2 → ℝ², IsPlanarStraightLineDrawing ⊤ f ∧
      ∀ u v, (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)).Adj u v → ∃ n : ℤ, dist (f u) (f v) = n := by
  have hf : Function.Injective fun i : Fin 2 => EuclideanSpace.single (0 : Fin 2) (i : ℝ) := by
    intro i j h
    simpa [Fin.ext_iff] using congrArg (· 0) h
  refine ⟨_, ⟨hf, fun u v huv => exists_path_segmentArcs hf huv, ?_, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
  · intro u v w huv hwu hwv
    fin_cases u <;> fin_cases v <;> fin_cases w <;> simp_all
  · intro u v u' v' huv huv' hne
    fin_cases u <;> fin_cases v <;> fin_cases u' <;> fin_cases v' <;> simp_all [Sym2.eq_swap]
  · intro u v huv
    refine ⟨1, ?_⟩
    fin_cases u <;> fin_cases v <;> simp_all [EuclideanSpace.dist_single_same]

claims.decomposer_note: "Drawn" means a planar straight-line (Fáry) drawing of a finite simple planar graph: an injective placement of vertices in ℝ² such that edges are straight segments that do not cross (and pass through no other vertices) and every edge has integer Euclidean length; by scaling this is equivalent to rational edge lengths, and since Mathlib has no planar-graph notion, planarity of the abstract graph (hypothesis) and of the drawing (conclusion) must both be defined explicitly.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates give equivalent, correct conclusions (injective placement in ℝ², closed edge segments avoiding other vertices, distinct edges meeting only at images of shared endpoints, integer Euclidean lengths); I verified the variants (open-segment form in c07, {f u, f v} ∩ {f w, f x} in c03/c05, set-inequality vs Sym2-inequality) are equivalent. The candidates split on the hypothesis: c01–c05, c07 define 'planar' as having a straight-line planar drawing (faithful only via Fáry's theorem), whereas c06 and c08 use the genuine topological definition (edges as simple arcs), which matches 'planar graph' literally. c08 is chosen over c06 because its straight-line drawing is literally a planar drawing with segment arcs (matching the article's wording 'planar drawing in which every edge is a straight segment'), it proves the redundant path condition is automatic and that straight-line drawings are planar drawings, and includes a K₂ test witnessing non-vacuity. context: In mathematics, Harborth's conjecture states that every planar graph has a planar drawing in which every edge is a straight segment of integer length. This conjecture is named after Heiko Harborth, and (if true) would strengthen Fáry's theorem on the existence of straight-line drawings for every planar graph. For this reason, a drawing with integer edge lengths is also known as an integral Fáry embedding. Despite much subsequent research, Harborth's conjecture remains unsolved.

decomposition_objections.text: None. The single slot matches the statement, and its notes (finite simple graph, injective placement, straight non-crossing segments avoiding other vertices, integer Euclidean lengths, explicit definitions of planarity for hypothesis and conclusion) were followed.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Harborth's conjecture

Harborth's conjecture states that every planar graph can be drawn with integer edge lengths:
every (finite, simple) planar graph has a planar drawing in the Euclidean plane in which every
edge is a straight line segment of integer length. Such a drawing is also called an
*integral Fáry embedding*, since (if true) the conjecture strengthens Fáry's theorem on the
existence of planar straight-line drawings.

Mathlib has no notion of a planar graph, so this file defines planar drawings explicitly.
A *planar drawing* of a graph maps vertices to distinct points of the plane and edges to simple
arcs joining the images of their endpoints, so that an arc contains no vertex other than its
endpoints and two distinct arcs meet only in common endpoints. A graph is *planar* if it has a
planar drawing. A *planar straight-line drawing* is a planar drawing in which the arc of every
edge is the closed segment between the images of its endpoints.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Harborth's conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harborth%27s_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in
  mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [KH01] Kemnitz, A. and Harborth, H., *Plane integral drawings of planar graphs*,
  Discrete Mathematics 236 (2001), 191–195.
  [doi:10.1016/S0012-365X(00)00442-8](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0012-365X(00)00442-8)
-/

namespace HarborthsConjecture

open scoped EuclideanGeometry

variable {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V)

/--
`IsPlanarDrawing G f arc` says that `f` and `arc` form a planar drawing of `G` in the plane:
* the vertices are mapped injectively to points `f v` of the plane;
* the edge `s(u, v)` is drawn as the set `arc s(u, v)`, which is a simple arc from `f u` to `f v`,
  i.e. the range of an injective path from `f u` to `f v`;
* the arc of an edge passes through no vertex other than its two endpoints;
* the arcs of two distinct edges meet only in the images of their common endpoints.
-/
structure IsPlanarDrawing (f : V → ℝ²) (arc : Sym2 V → Set ℝ²) : Prop where
  injective : Function.Injective f
  exists_path : ∀ u v, G.Adj u v →
    ∃ γ : Path (f u) (f v), Function.Injective γ ∧ Set.range γ = arc s(u, v)
  notMem_arc : ∀ u v w, G.Adj u v → w ≠ u → w ≠ v → f w ∉ arc s(u, v)
  inter_subset : ∀ u v u' v', G.Adj u v → G.Adj u' v' → s(u, v) ≠ s(u', v') →
    arc s(u, v) ∩ arc s(u', v') ⊆ f '' (({u, v} : Set V) ∩ {u', v'})

/-- A graph is planar if it has a planar drawing in the plane. -/
def IsPlanar : Prop :=
  ∃ (f : V → ℝ²) (arc : Sym2 V → Set ℝ²), IsPlanarDrawing G f arc

/-- The straight-line arcs of a vertex placement `f`: the unordered pair `s(u, v)` is sent to the
closed segment between `f u` and `f v`. -/
def segmentArcs (f : V → ℝ²) : Sym2 V → Set ℝ² :=
  Sym2.lift ⟨fun u v => segment ℝ (f u) (f v), fun _ _ => segment_symm ℝ _ _⟩

@[simp, category API, AMS 5 52]
theorem segmentArcs_mk (f : V → ℝ²) (u v : V) :
    segmentArcs f s(u, v) = segment ℝ (f u) (f v) :=
  rfl

/-- `IsPlanarStraightLineDrawing G f` says that placing the vertices of `G` at the points `f v`
and drawing every edge as a straight segment gives a planar drawing of `G`
(a *Fáry embedding* of `G`). -/
def IsPlanarStraightLineDrawing (f : V → ℝ²) : Prop :=
  IsPlanarDrawing G f (segmentArcs f)

variable {G}

/-- If the vertices are placed injectively, the segment of every edge is a simple arc between the
images of its endpoints, so the `exists_path` condition of `IsPlanarDrawing` is automatic for
straight-line drawings. -/
@[category API, AMS 5 52]
theorem exists_path_segmentArcs {f : V → ℝ²} (hf : Function.Injective f) {u v : V}
    (huv : G.Adj u v) :
    ∃ γ : Path (f u) (f v), Function.Injective γ ∧ Set.range γ = segmentArcs f s(u, v) :=
  ⟨Path.segment (f u) (f v), fun _ _ h => Subtype.ext <|
    AffineMap.lineMap_injective ℝ (hf.ne huv.ne) (by simpa using h), by simp⟩

/-- A graph with a planar straight-line drawing is planar. -/
@[category API, AMS 5 52]
theorem IsPlanarStraightLineDrawing.isPlanar {f : V → ℝ²}
    (hf : IsPlanarStraightLineDrawing G f) : IsPlanar G :=
  ⟨f, segmentArcs f, hf⟩

variable (G)

/--
**Harborth's conjecture.** Every planar graph can be drawn with integer edge lengths: every
finite planar graph $G$ has a planar drawing in the plane in which every edge is a straight
line segment whose Euclidean length is an integer.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 52]
theorem harborths_conjecture [Fintype V] (hG : IsPlanar G) :
    ∃ f : V → ℝ², IsPlanarStraightLineDrawing G f ∧
      ∀ u v, G.Adj u v → ∃ n : ℤ, dist (f u) (f v) = n := by
  sorry

/-- The complete graph on two vertices satisfies Harborth's conjecture: place the two vertices
at distance `1` apart. -/
@[category test, AMS 5 52]
theorem harborths_conjecture_completeGraph_fin_two :
    ∃ f : Fin 2 → ℝ², IsPlanarStraightLineDrawing ⊤ f ∧
      ∀ u v, (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)).Adj u v → ∃ n : ℤ, dist (f u) (f v) = n := by
  have hf : Function.Injective fun i : Fin 2 => EuclideanSpace.single (0 : Fin 2) (i : ℝ) := by
    intro i j h
    simpa [Fin.ext_iff] using congrArg (· 0) h
  refine ⟨_, ⟨hf, fun u v huv => exists_path_segmentArcs hf huv, ?_, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
  · intro u v w huv hwu hwv
    fin_cases u <;> fin_cases v <;> fin_cases w <;> simp_all
  · intro u v u' v' huv huv' hne
    fin_cases u <;> fin_cases v <;> fin_cases u' <;> fin_cases v' <;> simp_all [Sym2.eq_swap]
  · intro u v huv
    refine ⟨1, ?_⟩
    fin_cases u <;> fin_cases v <;> simp_all [EuclideanSpace.dist_single_same]

end HarborthsConjecture

items: Graphs are finite simple graphs: `{V : Type*} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V)`. The list entry says only "every planar graph"; the literature (Kemnitz–Harborth 2001, the Wikipedia article) concerns finite graphs, and the decomposition notes say finite.

Planarity of the abstract graph is defined topologically (the actual definition of a planar graph), not via Fáry straight-line drawings: `IsPlanarDrawing G f arc` requires f injective, each edge s(u,v) drawn as a simple arc (the range of an injective `Path (f u) (f v)`), arcs containing no vertex other than their endpoints, and arcs of distinct edges meeting only in images of common endpoints. `IsPlanar G := ∃ f arc, IsPlanarDrawing G f arc`. By Fáry's theorem this is equivalent to having a planar straight-line drawing, so a reviewer preferring the Fáry-based definition would obtain an equivalent statement.

The drawing in the conclusion is required to be planar (non-crossing), following the article's wording "planar drawing in which every edge is a straight segment"; a mere injective placement with integer distances would be a different (much weaker) statement. `IsPlanarStraightLineDrawing G f := IsPlanarDrawing G f (segmentArcs f)` where `segmentArcs f s(u,v) = segment ℝ (f u) (f v)` (closed segments, via `Sym2.lift` with `segment_symm`). Non-crossing means: closed segments of two distinct edges intersect only in the images of their common endpoints, and no segment contains a non-endpoint vertex.
The `exists_path` field is redundant for straight-line drawings (automatic once f is injective); this is proved as the API lemma `exists_path_segmentArcs`, so it does not alter the conjecture.

Integer edge length is `∃ n : ℤ, dist (f u) (f v) = n` with the Euclidean metric on `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)` (notation `ℝ²` from FormalConjecturesForMathlib.Geometry.2d). Lengths are automatically positive since f is injective; using ℕ would be equivalent. The article's equivalent rational-length version was not added as a separate variant.

Arcs are indexed by `Sym2 V` and constrained only on edges; the drawing predicate is agnostic about non-edges. Quantifying over ordered adjacent pairs (u,v) with `s(u,v)` is harmless since the required path from f u to f v reverses to one from f v to f u.

The bespoke definitions are kept in the problem file (single-file deliverable). A maintainer may prefer to move `IsPlanarDrawing`/`IsPlanar` to FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph since they are reusable.

Added API lemmas (`segmentArcs_mk`, `exists_path_segmentArcs`, `IsPlanarStraightLineDrawing.isPlanar`) and a `category test` lemma proving the conjecture's conclusion for K₂, which also witnesses that the hypothesis `IsPlanar` is satisfiable (non-vacuous).

reviewer_notes: No candidate omitted the slot; none of the candidates' reports raise objections. Ambiguity in the source: the list entry says only 'every planar graph can be drawn with integer edge lengths'; following the Wikipedia article and the decomposition notes, this is read as finite simple planar graphs and planar straight-line (Fáry) drawings with integer Euclidean edge lengths (the literal integer version, not the equivalent rational version). Hypothesis planarity is stated topologically ([Fintype V], edges as ranges of injective Paths, no vertex on a non-incident arc, distinct arcs meet only at common endpoints); the Fáry-based definitions used by c01–c05/c07 are equivalent by Fáry's theorem but less literal. Bespoke definitions (IsPlanarDrawing, IsPlanar, segmentArcs, IsPlanarStraightLineDrawing) live in the problem file under namespace HarborthsConjecture; a maintainer may prefer moving the planarity definitions to FormalConjecturesForMathlib. c01 additionally offered a Kleber variant and a cubic solved variant, outside the decomposition table, so not shipped.
